headline: Elon Musk has praised Micron for being reasonable on future memory prices and said other suppliers have been extortionate, without naming them.
score_reason: Pool score kept: the post is real and ties into the memory-price squeeze, but it carries no figures or named target.
importance_line: It shows how tense memory pricing has become, with a major buyer publicly rewarding one supplier and warning others, which could affect what carmakers, phone makers and AI firms pay for chips; Musk gave no figures or names, so the target and any actual price terms are unconfirmed.
summary: TrendForce reports that Elon Musk, chief executive of Tesla, wrote on X on 14 Oct 2026 that Micron, the US memory-chip maker, "has been reasonable regarding future memory prices, while others have been extortionate", and that customers "won't forget" such treatment; the Korean outlet Money Today says this sparked speculation about Samsung and SK hynix, though Musk named neither. The post comes as memory makers tie customers into long-term supply deals, and Reuters reports that Micron's commitments reached $32 billion by September, up from $22 billion in June.
notes: Speculation about the target comes from Money Today as cited by TrendForce; stated in the summary as speculation.
